claim: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by irreversible alveolar damage and lung tissue fibrosis.
source: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a lethal disease of unknown etiology, characterized by irreversible alveolar damage and lung tissue fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as an established characteristic of IPF in the introduction, drawing from established scientific knowledge about the disease.

claim: The progression of IPF leads to persistent decline of lung function, attenuated exercise ability, impaired quality of life and eventually death within 3~5 years after disease onset.
source: The progression of IPF would lead to persistent decline of lung function, attenuated exercise ability, impaired quality of life and eventually death within 3~5 years after disease onset (Raghu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Raghu et al., 2022.

claim: There is currently no cure for IPF.
source: Currently, there is no cure for IPF, and the clinically applied treatments, such as self-care measures, anti-fibrotic medication, and pulmonary rehabilitation, can only help relieve the symptoms and/or slow down the progression of IPF.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about current IPF treatment limitations.

claim: Nintedanib and Pirfenidone reduce the rate of decline in lung function (primarily lung forced vital capacity) rather than halt or reverse IPF disease progression.
source: Among them, the first-line anti-fibrotic drugs Nintedanib and Pirfenidone could only reduce the rate of decline in lung function (primarily lung forced vital capacity) rather than halt or reverse the disease progression.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about these drugs and is consistent with the citations provided in the surrounding text.

claim: Patients with IPF may discontinue Nintedanib and Pirfenidone due to adverse events such as nausea and diarrhea.
source: Furthermore, patients with IPF may discontinue Nintedanib and Pirfenidone due to adverse events such as nausea and diarrhea (Vancheri et al., 2018; Flaherty et al., 2018; Milger et al., 2015; Richeldi et al., 2014; Noble et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: Conventional IPF medications cannot repair or regenerate injured lung tissues in IPF patients.
source: More importantly, none of these conventional medications could repair or regenerate the injured lung tissues in IPF patients.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the limitations of conventional IPF treatments.

claim: P63+ airway basal progenitor cells are marked by the expression of TP63 (P63) and keratin 5 (KRT5).
source: Among these cell populations, airway basal stem/progenitor cells marked by the expression of TP63 (P63), keratin 5 (KRT5) have been widely studied (Zuo et al., 2015; Vaughan et al., 2015; Kumar et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: P63+ progenitor cells are capable of differentiating into secretory, goblet and ciliated cells and reconstituting the airway epithelium.
source: These P63+ progenitor cells located in the airway basal layer are known to be capable of differentiating into secretory, goblet and ciliated cells and reconstituting the airway epithelium (Davis and Wypych, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Davis and Wypych, 2021.

claim: P63+ progenitor cells can be activated by multiple types of major alveolar injuries including IPF, influenza infection, and COVID-19.
source: In the recent decade, it has been discovered that these P63+ progenitor cells in airway can be activated by multiple types of major alveolar injuries (eg. IPF, influenza infection, COVID-19), and then migrate from airway to the damaged loci in the alveolar compartment, where they play complex roles in the pathogenesis process (Zuo et al., 2015; Vaughan et al., 2015; Heydemann et al., 2023; Prasse et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Normal P63+ progenitor cells in the alveolar area can expand and rapidly form epithelial barriers to 'band-aid' injured lung tissue.
source: It is proposed that the normal P63+ progenitor cells in the alveolar area are able to expand and rapidly form epithelial barriers to 'band-aid' the injured lung tissue (Kumar et al., 2011; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kumar et al., 2011 and Zacharias et al., 2018.

claim: P63+ progenitor cells can differentiate towards alveolar epithelium lineages when stimulated by proper microenvironment signals.
source: When stimulated by proper microenvironment signals, the P63+ progenitor cells could also differentiate towards alveolar epithelium lineages to facilitate lung repair and regeneration (Zuo et al., 2015; Vaughan et al., 2015; Xi et al., 2017; Kathiriya et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Dysplastic P63+ progenitor cells are distributed near fibrotic foci in IPF patients and might be pro-fibrotic with potential to exacerbate IPF disease.
source: However, in the context of IPF, it has been confirmed that there are some dysplastic P63+ progenitor cells distributed near the fibrotic foci, which might be pro-fibrotic with potential to exacerbate the IPF disease (Habermann et al., 2020; Jaeger et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Habermann et al., 2020; Jaeger et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023.

claim: Transplanted mouse/human P63+ progenitor cells can engraft into injured mouse lung tissue, re-establish epithelial barrier, reconstitute vascularized air sac, and improve blood oxygen levels in a bleomycin-injured pulmonary fibrosis murine model.
source: The transplanted mouse/human P63+ progenitor cells were able to engraft into the injured mouse lung tissue, re-establish the epithelial barrier, reconstitute vascularized air sac, and improve the blood oxygen levels of the mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous preclinical studies (Shi et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2021) mentioned in the surrounding text.

claim: Transplantation of P63+ progenitor cells can attenuate collagen deposition and myofibroblast cell proliferation in lung and reduce mouse mortality in a bleomycin-injured pulmonary fibrosis murine model.
source: Transplantation of P63+ progenitor cells could also attenuate collagen deposition and myofibroblast cell proliferation in lung and eventually reduce mouse mortality (Shi et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shi et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2021.

claim: Pre-clinical safety evaluations showed that intrapulmonary transplantation of P63+ progenitor cells is very safe in mice and monkeys following Good Laboratory Practice guidelines.
source: Pre-clinical safety evaluations were also performed on both mice and monkeys following Good Laboratory Practice guidelines, showing that intrapulmonary transplantation of P63+ progenitor cells is very safe (Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2021.

claim: In a 2016 pilot clinical study, two patients with severe non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis treated with autologous P63+ progenitor cell transplantation showed remarkable pulmonary function recovery with no aberrant cell growth or other related adverse events.
source: In a pilot clinical study conducted in 2016, two patients with severe non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis were treated with autologous P63+ progenitor cell transplantation. Pulmonary functions of both patients recovered remarkably, with none aberrant cell growth or other related adverse events (AEs) during the whole follow-up time (Ma et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ma et al., 2018.

claim: In a controlled phase 1 clinical trial, autologous P63+ progenitor cell transplantation significantly improved gas transfer function (DLCO) in 17 COPD patients.
source: In a very recent report of a controlled phase 1 clinical trial, autologous P63+ progenitor cell transplantation was performed to treat 17 patients with chronic pulmonary obstructive disease (COPD). These data indicated that the cell treatment could significantly improve the gas transfer function (DLCO) of the COPD lung (Wang et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2024.

claim: This is the first clinical trial treating IPF patients with autologous P63+ lung progenitor cell product (REGEND001) transplantation.
source: Here, we report the first clinical trial treating IPF patients with autologous P63+ lung progenitor cell product (REGEND001) transplantation.
evidence: This is stated as a factual claim about the novelty of the current study.

claim: The clinical trial was an open-label, dose-escalation, phase I study conducted at three clinical research centers in China.
source: An open-label, dose-escalation, phase I clinical trial (CTR20210349, translated English version in Supplementary Material) was conducted at three clinical research centers (Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Shanghai Ruijin Hospital, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University) in China to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of treating IPF patients through autologous P63+ basal progenitor cell transplantation at different dosages.
evidence: This is a description of the study design and is supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The trial was approved by the National Medical Products Administration and the ethics committees of the three clinical research centers.
source: This trial was approved by the National Medical Products Administration and the ethic committee of the three clinical research centers, and was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and the principles of Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
evidence: This is stated as a factual claim about regulatory approval.

claim: Eligible patients were adults between ages 50 and 75 diagnosed with IPF based on 2018 guidelines.
source: Eligible patients were adults between the ages of 50 and 75 who were diagnosed with IPF based on the 2018 guidelines for diagnosis of IPF by the Pulmonary Pathology Society.
evidence: This describes the inclusion criteria for the study.

claim: Eligible patients had a DLCO between 30 to 79% of predicted value and FVC of 50% or more of predicted value.
source: Additional eligibility criteria were a DLCO that was 30 to 79% of the predicted value, a FVC that was 50% or more of the predicted value in pulmonary function tests within the preceding 3 months of patients screening.
evidence: This describes the inclusion criteria for the study.

claim: Patients were assigned to receive a single administration of autologous P63+ lung progenitor cells at 0.6x10^6, 1x10^6, 2x10^6, or 3.3x10^6 cells/kg bodyweight.
source: Patients were assigned to receive a single administration of autologous P63+ lung progenitor cells at 0.6x106, 1x106, 2x106, or 3.3x106 cells/kg bodyweight.
evidence: This describes the dose escalation design of the study.

claim: P63+ progenitor cells are selectively expanded through a pharmaceutical-grade cell cloning culture system.
source: P63+ progenitor cells are selectively expanded through a pharmaceutical-grade cell cloning culture system.
evidence: This describes the manufacturing method used in the study.

claim: 50 μg/mL gentamicin sulfate is applied at the initial passage but not in subsequent 2-5 passages to prevent microbial contamination.
source: 50 μg/mL gentamicin sulfate is applied at the initial passage but not in the subsequent 2–5 passages to prevent microbial contamination.
evidence: This describes the cell culture protocol used in the study.

claim: Each batch of cell products was confirmed to be free of bacterial and mycoplasma contamination, endotoxin, BSA, and antibiotic residues.
source: Each batch of cell products were confirmed to be free of bacterial and mycoplasma contamination, or endotoxin, BSA, and antibiotic residues.
evidence: This describes the quality control testing performed on the cell product.

claim: The primary outcome was the incidence and severity of cell therapy-related adverse events within 24 weeks after treatment.
source: The primary outcome of the study was the incidence and severity of the cell therapy-related AEs within 24 weeks after treatment.
evidence: This describes the primary endpoint of the study.

claim: Secondary outcome measures included DLCO-SB, FVC, DLCO/VA, 6MWD, and SGRQ at 4, 12, and 24 weeks after treatment.
source: evaluation of cell therapy efficacy through DLCO-SB, FVC, DLCO/VA, exercise tolerance test (6MWD), quality-of-life questionnaire SGRQ at 4 weeks, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks after treatment
evidence: This describes the secondary endpoints of the study.

claim: Twelve patients were enrolled in the trial from July 19, 2021 to June 9, 2023.
source: We conducted an open-label, dose-escalation phase 1 clinical trial (CTR20210349) from July 19, 2021 to June 9, 2023, to study the safety and efficacy of autologous P63+ lung progenitor cell transplantation in patients with IPF.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the study enrollment period.

claim: Twelve patients were assigned to one of four dose groups sequentially: 0.6 M, 1 M, 2 M, and 3.3 M cells/kg bodyweight.
source: Totally 12 patients were enrolled in the trial and assigned to one of four dose groups sequentially: 0.6 million cells/kg bodyweight (0.6 M), 1 million cells/kg bodyweight (1 M), 2 million cells/kg bodyweight (2 M), and 3.3 million cells/kg bodyweight (3.3 M; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the dose escalation design and patient allocation.

claim: 75% of trial participants used anti-fibrotic drug pirfenidone as concomitant medication.
source: Of note, 75% participants used anti-fibrotic drug pirfenidone as concomitant medication in this trial.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1 showing 9 out of 12 patients used pirfenidone.

claim: None of the participants used Nintedanib as concomitant medication.
source: None of them used Nintedanib as concomitant medication.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Tissue samples were collected from grade 3-5 bronchi of upper lung lobes in IPF patients.
source: First, a small tissue sample is collected via bronchoscopy from grade 3–5 bronchi of upper lung lobes in patients with IPF.
evidence: This describes the tissue sampling procedure used in the study.

claim: In IPF patients, fibrotic foci are mainly distributed in lower or middle lobes.
source: In IPF patients, the fibrotic foci are mainly distributed in lower or middle lobes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IPF pathology.

claim: Relatively healthy lung upper lobes were selected to collect tissue samples to obtain normal autologous P63+ progenitor cells instead of pro-fibrotic cells.
source: We selected relatively healthy lung upper lobes to collect tissue samples, which allowed us to collect the normal autologous P63+ progenitor cells instead of those pro-fibrotic cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the rationale for the sampling location and is supported by Figure 1B.

claim: KRT5+ cell purity was >95% as confirmed by flow cytometric analysis.
source: Expression of representative progenitor cell markers KRT5 and P63 was confirmed by immunofluorescence staining and flow cytometric analysis demonstrating KRT5+ cell purity >95% (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: No tumorigenic potential was confirmed in soft agar colony formation assay for each batch of cell product.
source: For each batch of cell product, no tumorigenic potential was confirmed in the soft agar colony formation assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the soft agar assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Progenitor cells cloned from different individual patients exhibited diverse morphology.
source: We noticed that the cell cloned from different individual patients exhibited diverse morphology: some clones were regularly round while others exhibited irregular shape (Figure 1D).
evidence: This observation is supported by the images shown in Figure 1D.

claim: There is a significant negative correlation between patient age and P63+ progenitor cell clone roundness.
source: The data revealed significant negative correlation between the age of patients and P63+ progenitor cell clone roundness, which might be related to previous findings that aging can negatively impact cell properties (Moreno-Valladares et al., 2023; Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2A and cited literature.

claim: There is a positive correlation between P63+ progenitor cell clone roundness and pulmonary function indexes DLCO, FVC, and FEV1.
source: Interestingly, we also observed a positive correlation between P63+ progenitor cell clone roundness and the pulmonary function indexes DLCO, FVC, and FEV1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Single-cell sequencing uncovered three distinct subpopulations: C1, C2, and C3.
source: Unsupervised clustering of the cells uncovered three distinct subpopulations:C1, C2, and C3 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The C1 population is characterized by lung progenitor classic markers KRT5 and P63 and accounts for 65.03% of all cells.
source: The C1 population was characterized by lung progenitor classic markers KRT5 and P63 and accounts for more than half of all cells (65.03%; Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: C1 cells demonstrate high expression of genes involved in Wnt Signaling pathway and negative regulation of apoptotic signaling pathway.
source: Gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes showed that C1 cells demonstrated high expression of genes involved in Wnt Signaling pathway and negative regulation of apoptotic signaling pathway, which is crucial for maintaining the identity of stem cells and the development of the lung (Frank et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2D and cited literature.

claim: C1 cells demonstrate function of positive regulation of angiogenesis and negative regulation of fibroblast proliferation.
source: Notably, C1 cells also demonstrate the function of positive regulation of angiogenesis and negative regulation of fibroblast proliferation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The C2 population accounts for 23.40% of total cells and expresses KRT5, P63, and proliferation-related marker KI67.
source: The C2 populations accounts for 23.40% of the total number of cells. It also expressed KRT5, P63, and meanwhile expresses the proliferation-related marker KI67 (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: C2 cells are mainly enriched in mitosis-related genes, consistent with their identity as a proliferative state.
source: C2 was mainly enriched in mitosis-related genes, which is consistent with its identity as a proliferative state (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: C3 cells account for 11.57% of total cells and show very low level of KRT5 or P63 expression but high level of AEC1 gene HOPX.
source: C3 cells accounts for 11.57% of the total number of cells, which showed very low level of KRT5 or P63 expression, but expressed high level of alveolar epithelial cell types 1 (AEC1) gene HOPX.
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: C3 cells express a set of genes known as markers for variant progenitor cells, including CXCL17, CEACAM6, IL1RN, and CLDN4.
source: Of note, the C3 cells also expressed a set of genes known as markers for variant progenitor cells, including CXCL17, CEACAM6, IL1RN, and CLDN4 (Figure 2E; Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by the feature plots shown in Figure 2E and cited literature.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in C3 cells are enriched in epithelial cell development and differentiation and wound healing.
source: Further gene ontology analysis identified differentially expressed genes in C3 cells were enriched in epithelial cell development and differentiation and wound healing (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Basal cells isolated from injured area of IPF lungs are significantly enriched with genes related to DNA damage, senescence, apoptosis, and differentiation of mesenchymal cells and fibroblasts compared to C3 cells from healthy area.
source: The data showed that in comparison to the C3 cells isolated from healthy area, the basal cells isolated from injured area were significantly enriched with genes related to DNA damage, senescence, apoptosis, as well as genes related to the differentiation of mesenchymal cells and fibroblasts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis comparing C3 cells to basal cells from injured areas, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The C3 cells are different from pro-fibrotic basal cells found in injured areas of IPF lungs.
source: Therefore, the C3 cells are different from those pro-fibrotic basal cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gene expression profiles between C3 cells and basal cells from injured areas.

claim: The current cell isolation and expansion system can efficiently enrich normal P63+ lung progenitor cells from IPF patients.
source: Altogether these data indicated that the current cell isolation and expansion system could efficiently enrich normal P63+ lung progenitor cells from IPF patients.
evidence: This is inferred from the single-cell sequencing data showing the composition of the cell product.

claim: Patients were followed up at baseline, 1 week, 4 weeks, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks post REGEND001 treatment for safety evaluation.
source: Patients were followed up at baseline, 1 week, 4 weeks, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks post REGEND001 treatment for safety evaluation.
evidence: This describes the follow-up schedule for the study.

claim: Until 24 weeks after transplantation, 62 cases of grade I-III adverse events were recorded, with no grade IV and grade V AEs.
source: Until 24 weeks after transplantation, totally 62 cases of grade I-III adverse events (AEs), but no grade IV and grade V AEs, were recorded (Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data presented in Table 2.

claim: The most common adverse event was COVID-19, recorded in all 6 patients in 2 M and 3.3 M dose groups.
source: The most common AE is COVID-19. COVID-19 were recorded in all 6 patients in 2 M and 3.3 M dose groups, which were not related to cell therapy but due to the outbreak of pandemic in China from December 2022 to March 2023.
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data and the temporal context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

claim: 22.6% (14/62) of adverse events were considered related to cell therapy.
source: 22.6% (14/62) AEs were considered related to the cell therapy.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the adverse event data.

claim: Fever was one of the most common cell therapy-related AEs (21.4%, 1 grade II, 2 grade I), occurring within 24 hr after treatment and recovering 4-9 hr afterwards.
source: Fever is one of the mostly common cell therapy-related AEs (21.4%, 1 grade II, 2 grade I), which all happened within 24 hr after REGEND001 treatment and recovered 4–9 hr afterwards.
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data.

claim: Bloody sputum was a common cell therapy-related AE (21.4%, all grade I), occurring within 24 hr after treatment and recovering within 1-3 days.
source: Bloody sputum is another common cell therapy-related AEs (21.4%, all grade I), which all happened within 24 hr after REGEND001 treatment and recovered within 1–3 days.
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data.

claim: The reason for bloody sputum was considered to be related to bronchoscopic surgery but not the cell product.
source: The reason for bloody sputum was considered to be related to the bronchoscopic surgery but not the cell product.
evidence: This is a clinical judgment made by the investigators based on the timing and nature of the adverse event.

claim: Grade III AEs included 2 severe COVID-19 cases and 2 acute bronchitis cases.
source: The grade III AEs include 2 severe COVID-19 and 2 acute bronchitis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data.

claim: Two acute bronchitis cases occurred in two patients at 2 months and 4 months post cell transplantation and both recovered after standard treatment.
source: The 2 acute bronchitis happened in two patients in 2 months and 4 months post cell transplantation respectively, and both recovered after standard treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the adverse event data.

claim: The acute bronchitis cases were not related to cell treatment based on medical history of the two patients.
source: Considering the medical history of the two patients, we think the acute bronchitis were not related to the cell treatment.
evidence: This is a clinical judgment made by the investigators.

claim: No clinically meaningful change of 4 tumor markers in blood sample was observed.
source: Consistently, no clinically meaningful change of 4 tumor markers in blood sample was observed (Appendix 1—figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the tumor marker data shown in Appendix 1—figure 3.

claim: No signs of malignancy or new pathologies were found in any patient by consecutive high-resolution CT scanning of the chest.
source: By consecutive high-resolution CT (HRCT) scanning of the chest, we did not find any signs of malignancy or new pathologies in any patient.
evidence: This claim is supported by the CT imaging data.

claim: Autologous P63+ progenitor cell transplantation therapy had an acceptable safety profile among IPF patients.
source: Altogether these data indicated that autologous P63+ progenitor cells transplantation therapy had an acceptable safety profile among IPF patients.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the safety data presented in the study.

claim: DLCO is a consistent and strong predictor of mortality in patients with various fibrotic lung diseases.
source: In patients with IPF, progression of pulmonary fibrosis is the primary cause of decline in gas transfer function, which is a consistent and strong predictor of mortality in patients with various fibrotic lung diseases (Raghu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Raghu et al., 2022.

claim: Seven patients in higher dose groups (1.0~3.3 M) showed statistically significant increase of DLCO/VA level from 72.06% (baseline) to 84.10% (24 weeks) of predicted value (p-value = 0.008).
source: In current trial, we found that the 7 patients in the higher dose groups (1.0~3.3 M) showed statistically significant increase of DLCO/VA level trend from averagely 72.06% (baseline) to 84.10% (24 weeks) of predicted value (p-value = 0.008).
evidence: This claim is supported by the efficacy data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The overall change of DLCO/VA in the higher dose group was statistically significant from that in the lower dose group (p-value = 0.019).
source: Of note, the overall change of DLCO/VA in the higher dose group was statistically significant from that in the lower dose group (p-value = 0.019), indicating a dose-dependent therapeutic effect (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the efficacy data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: REGEND001 treatment had potential to improve lung gas transfer function when applied at higher dose.
source: Altogether, above data indicated that REGEND001 treatment had potential to improve lung gas transfer function when applied at higher dose.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the DLCO/VA efficacy data.

claim: Concomitant COVID-19 events in 2 M and 3.3 M groups post cell treatment might compromise some potential benefit from REGEND001 treatment.
source: Moreover, we also noticed that the concomitant COVID-19 events happened in 2 M and 3.3 M group post cell treatment, which might compromise some the potential benefit from REGEND001 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of COVID-19 infections and the efficacy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: FVC decline is an indicator of IPF progression.
source: FVC represents the airflow aspect of lung function, and its decline is the indicator of the progression of IPF (Fainberg et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fainberg et al., 2022.

claim: In higher dose groups, minimal improvement of FVC% from 76.91% (baseline) to 77.01% (24 weeks) was observed.
source: Unlike DLCO, in the higher dose groups, we only observed minimal improvement of FVC% from averagely 76.91% (baseline) to 77.01% (24 weeks).
evidence: This claim is supported by the FVC efficacy data.

claim: The overall change of FVC in the higher dose group was statistically significant from that in the lower dose group (p=0.028).
source: The overall change of FVC in the higher dose group was statistically significant from that in the lower dose group (p=0.028; Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the FVC efficacy data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In higher dose groups, three of seven patients demonstrated >2% positive change of FVC% after REGEND001 treatment, reaching the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for FVC% change in IPF patients.
source: In the higher dose groups, three of seven patients demonstrated >2% positive change of FVC% after REGEND001 treatment, which reached the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for FVC% change in IPF patients (du Bois et al., 2011a).
evidence: This claim is supported by the FVC efficacy data and cited literature defining MCID.

claim: REGEND001 treatment might have potential to stabilize or slightly improve FVC when given at high dose.
source: Altogether, these data suggested that REGEND001 treatment might have potential to stabilize or slightly improve FVC when given at a high dose.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FVC efficacy data.

claim: Patients in higher dose groups demonstrated statistically significant improvement of 6MWD from 424 m at baseline to 482 m at 24 weeks (p-value = 0.008).
source: In consistent with their improvement of lung functions, patients in higher dose groups demonstrated statistically significant improvement of 6MWD from averagely 424 m at baseline to 482 m at 24 weeks (p-value = 0.008; Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the 6MWD efficacy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The 58 m increase of 6MWD is considered clinically quite meaningful.
source: The 58 m increase of 6MWD is considered clinically quite meaningful (du Bois et al., 2011c).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to du Bois et al., 2011c defining clinically meaningful change in 6MWD.

claim: Patients in higher dose groups demonstrated decrease of SGRQ score from mean 32.3 at baseline to 25.8 at 24 weeks.
source: Similar to the 6MWD result, patients in higher dose groups demonstrated decrease of SGRQ numerically from mean 32.3 at baseline to 25.8 at 24 weeks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the SGRQ data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 6 points change of SGRQ score is considered clinically quite meaningful.
source: The 6 points change of SGRQ score were considered clinically quite meaningful (Kang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kang et al., 2021 defining clinically meaningful change in SGRQ.

claim: REGEND001 treatment, especially at higher dose groups, could help improve exercise ability and quality of life in IPF patients.
source: Altogether, these findings suggest that REGEND001 treatment, especially at higher dose groups, could help to improve the exercise ability and quality of life in IPF patients.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 6MWD and SGRQ efficacy data.

claim: Honeycombing pattern in CT imaging is considered permanent and independently associated with IPF disease prognosis.
source: The honeycombing pattern in CT imaging is considered permanent and independently associated with the disease prognosis (Raghu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Raghu et al., 2022.

claim: At baseline, all recruited IPF patients showed predominantly peripheral and lower lobe bilateral reticulation and honeycombing pattern.
source: The results indicated that at baseline, all recruited IPF patients shows predominantly peripheral and lower lobe bilateral reticulation and honeycombing pattern.
evidence: This is based on the CT imaging evaluation by three experts.

claim: Patient #303 and #305 in 1 M group demonstrated resolution of honeycombing lesion in their lower lungs at 24 weeks.
source: At 24 weeks, as most patients showed no obvious change of lung CT images post cell therapy, the Patient #303 and #305 in 1 M group demonstrated resolution of honeycombing lesion in their lower lungs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the CT imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 3D computational visualization of #305 CT images showed that improvement of lung lesion was exclusively observed in the lower lobes.
source: We also performed three-dimensional (3D) computational visualization of reticulation and honeycombing in #305 CT images. Interestingly, the 3D data showed that the improvement of lung lesion was exclusively observed in the lower lobes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the 3D CT visualization shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cell suspension delivered through bronchoscope tends to flow into lower lobes due to gravity, resulting in cell concentration in lower lobes.
source: One explanation could be that the cell suspension delivered through the bronchoscope tend to flow into the lower lobes due to gravity, which would result in cell concentration in lower lobes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed pattern of improvement in lower lobes.

claim: Patients #303 and #305 demonstrated improvement of DLCO, FVC, and 6MWD consistent with their CT image improvement.
source: In consistency with the improvement of CT images in #303 and #305, these two patients demonstrated improvement of DLCO, FVC, and 6MWD as well (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the efficacy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: High clone roundness morphology might not be required for therapeutic efficacy based on cells from #303 and #305 having vastly diverse roundness.
source: Interestingly, based on the data in Figure 2, the cell cloned from #303 and #305 had vastly diverse roundness, suggesting that high clone roundness morphology might not be required for therapeutic efficacy.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that both patients showed efficacy despite different cell morphologies.

claim: REGEND001 treatment has potential to repair pulmonary fibrotic structure at least in some patients in 1 M group.
source: Altogether the above data suggested that REGEND001 treatment have potential to repair the pulmonary fibrotic structure at least in some patients in 1 M group.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CT imaging and functional data for patients #303 and #305.

claim: Destruction of alveolar tissues in IPF patients' lungs is currently irreversible.
source: The destruction of alveolar tissues in the lungs of IPF patients is currently irreversible.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IPF.

claim: Human P63+ lung progenitor cells can be easily isolated, expanded, and transplanted for lung regeneration.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that human P63+ lung progenitor cells can be easily isolated, expanded, and transplanted for lung regeneration (Ma et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2018 and Wang et al., 2024.

claim: Apart from KRT5+/P63+ basal progenitor cells, a subpopulation of 'variant progenitor cells' was identified in IPF patients.
source: Interestingly, apart from the KRT5+/P63+ basal progenitor cells, we also identified a subpopulation of 'variant progenitor cells' in IPF patients.
evidence: This is based on the single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in the study.

claim: Variant cells have been found in healthy donors in low numbers and in injured lobes of IPF patients with high abundance.
source: Similar variant cells have been found in healthy donors in low numbers as well as in the injured lobes of IPF patients with high abundance (Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2023.

claim: Cells cloned from healthy lobe have a low abundance of variant cells like those cloned from healthy donors.
source: Interestingly, our cells cloned from healthy lobe have a low abundance of variant cells exactly like those cloned from healthy donors (Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the single-cell RNA sequencing data with cited literature.

claim: The variant progenitor cells in this study exhibited higher expression of HOPX gene and lower expression of fibrosis-related genes compared to previously reported pro-fibrotic subpopulation in IPF patients.
source: Moreover, unlike the previously reported pro-fibrotic subpopulation in IPF patients, our variant progenitor cells exhibited a higher expression level of the HOPX gene, which is known to be expressed in normal type I alveolar cells, while exhibited lower expression of fibrosis-related genes (Heinzelmann et al., 2022).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the single-cell RNA sequencing data with cited literature.

claim: Relatively normal, but not pro-fibrotic, progenitor cells can be cloned from healthy lobes of IPF patients for manufacturing a qualified cell therapeutic product.
source: These data suggest that we can clone relatively normal, but not pro-fibrotic, progenitor cells from the healthy lobes of IPF patients, which can be used to manufacture a qualified cell therapeutic product.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the single-cell RNA sequencing data comparing cells from healthy vs injured lobes.

claim: Abnormal, dysplastic P63+ progenitor cells located in injured lung area of IPF patients could halt repair process, participate in 'honeycomb' structure formation and be deleterious for lung function.
source: Some previous studies also proposed that those abnormal, dysplastic P63+ progenitor cells located in the injured lung area of IPF patients could halt the repair process, participate in 'honeycomb' structure formation and be deleterious for the lung function (Jaeger et al., 2022; Hewitt et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jaeger et al., 2022 and Hewitt et al., 2023.

claim: The safety data indicated minimal safety issues, with all events related to cell administration being mild and transient.
source: Our data indicated minimal safety issues, with all events related to cell administration being mild and transient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the safety data presented in the study.

claim: P63+ progenitor cells isolated from healthy lobes of IPF patients are safe for intrapulmonary transplantation.
source: Considering our previous pre-clinical animal data altogether (Zhou et al., 2021), we now know that at least the P63+ progenitor cells isolated from the healthy lobes of IPF patients are safe for intrapulmonary transplantation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the safety data in the current study combined with previous preclinical data.

claim: DLCO is a consistent and powerful predictor of mortality in patients with various fibrotic lung diseases including IPF.
source: DLCO is considered to be a consistent and powerful predictor of mortality in patients with various fibrotic lung diseases including IPF (Raghu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Raghu et al., 2022.

claim: Low DLCO levels are strongly associated with diminished survival rate.
source: Low DLCO level are strongly associated with diminished survival rate (Latsi et al., 2003; Fell et al., 2009; du Bois et al., 2011b; Ley et al., 2011; Song et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: A drop of more than 15% in DLCO was associated with a threefold increased risk of death compared to a drop of less than 15% in IPF patients.
source: A drop of more than 15% in DLCO was associated with a threefold increased risk of death compared to a drop of less than 15% in IPF patients (Doubková et al., 2018; Collard et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Doubková et al., 2018 and Collard et al., 2003.

claim: DLCO has a predictive effect on exercise ability of IPF patients.
source: Additionally, DLCO also has a predictive effect on the exercise ability of IPF patients (Fernández Fabrellas et al., 2018; Lei et al., 2022; Smyth et al., 2023; Silva et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: Conventional anti-fibrotic drugs could not achieve improvements in DLCO in IPF patients.
source: Earlier studies indicated that conventional anti-fibrotic drugs could not achieve improvements in DLCO in IPF patients.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from earlier studies.

claim: Durheim et al. reported an annual change rate of predicted DLCO% of –2.9% in 436 IPF patients after initiating antifibrotic therapy.
source: In a clinical trial of conventional IPF treatment, Durheim et al. analyzed data from 436 IPF patients after initiating antifibrotic therapy and reported an annual change rate of predicted DLCO% of –2.9% (Durheim et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Durheim et al., 2021.

claim: Zulkova et al. found that the predicted mean change in DLCO% at week 24 was –1.6% when evaluating pirfenidone effect in 383 IPF patients.
source: Similarly, when Zulkova et al. evaluated the effect of pirfenidone on lung function decline and survival based on 383 patients with IPF, they found that the predicted mean change in DLCO% at week 24 was –1.6% (Zurkova et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zurkova et al., 2019.

claim: The current study demonstrated a +12.0% increase in DLCO/VA% and a +5.4% increase in DLCO% from baseline at 24 weeks in higher dose groups.
source: In contrast, our study demonstrated a+12.0% increase in DLCO/VA% and a+5.4% increase in DLCO% from baseline at 24 weeks in higher dose groups.
evidence: This is based on the efficacy data presented in the study.

claim: The DLCO improvement in higher dose groups implies a potential advantage over conventional therapy, showing statistically significant difference from patients in lower dose group.
source: Although there were data from only 7 patients in the higher dose groups, it still implies a potential advantage over conventional therapy, showing a statistically significant difference from patients in the lower dose group.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparison of the efficacy data with conventional therapy outcomes from literature.

claim: The sample size of the study was very small.
source: Firstly, the sample size of the study was very small.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a limitation of the study.

claim: The absence of a placebo-controlled arm makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions about treatment efficacy.
source: Secondly, the absence of a placebo-controlled arm makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions about the efficacy of the treatment.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a limitation of the study design.

claim: Progenitor cells cloned from individual patients had their own morphological properties and genetic/epigenetic background, which might lead to distinct response to therapy in different individuals.
source: Thirdly, the progenitor cells cloned from individual patients had their own morphological properties as well as genetic and epigenetic background, which might lead to distinct response to therapy in different individuals.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a limitation based on the observed variability in cell morphology and patient responses.

claim: Data collection and analysis of 2 M and 3.3 M patient groups were interfered by concomitant COVID-19 events and city lockdown policy.
source: Fourthly, the data collection and analysis of the 2 M and 3.3 M patient groups were interfered by the concomitant COVID-19 events and city lockdown policy.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a limitation of the study.

claim: A randomized, placebo-controlled, blind, multi-center phase 2 study with larger sample size is currently being performed in China (Clinical Trial No. NCT06081621).
source: To overcome some of these limitations, a randomized, placebo-controlled, blind, multi-center phase 2 study with a larger sample size is currently being performed in China (Clinical Trial No. NCT06081621).
evidence: This is stated as a factual claim about an ongoing follow-up study.

claim: P63+ basal progenitor cell was safe and tolerated at all doses, with no dose-limiting toxicity or cell therapy-related severe adverse events observed.
source: P63+ basal progenitor cell was safe and tolerated at all doses, with no dose-limiting toxicity or cell therapy-related severe adverse events observed.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the safety results.

claim: Patients in three higher dose groups showed significant improvement of lung gas transfer function as well as exercise ability.
source: Patients in three higher dose groups showed significant improvement of lung gas transfer function as well as exercise ability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the efficacy results.

claim: Resolution of honeycomb lesion was observed in patients of higher dose groups.
source: Resolution of honeycomb lesion was observed in patients of higher dose groups.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the imaging results.

claim: REGEND001 has high safety profile and encourages further efficacy exploration in IPF patients.
source: REGEND001 has high safety profile and meanwhile encourages further efficacy exploration in IPF patients.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Progenitor cells were isolated from a trace amount of healthy airway epithelium sample obtained via bronchoscopic brushing.
source: The progenitor cells were isolated from a trace amount of healthy airway epithelium sample obtained via bronchoscopic brushing.
evidence: This describes the cell isolation procedure used in the study.

claim: After 3-5 weeks of cell expansion, up to 100 million P63+ lung progenitor cells were produced.
source: After 3–5 weeks of cell expansion, up to 100 million P63+ lung progenitor cells were produced and transplanted into the lungs of IPF patients via bronchoscopy.
evidence: This describes the cell manufacturing process used in the study.

claim: Cells were transplanted into lungs of IPF patients via bronchoscopy.
source: After 3–5 weeks of cell expansion, up to 100 million P63+ lung progenitor cells were produced and transplanted into the lungs of IPF patients via bronchoscopy.
evidence: This describes the cell transplantation procedure used in the study.

claim: Nintedanib was excluded from allowed medication list because as tyrosine kinase inhibitor, it is worried to have growth inhibition effect on transplanted progenitor cells.
source: Nintedanib was excluded from the allowed medication list because as tyrosine kinase inhibitor, it is worried to have growth inhibition effect on the transplanted progenitor cells.
evidence: This explains the rationale for excluding Nintedanib from concomitant medications.
